content.title: About
content.content: Berries are edible fruits of various shrubs and herbaceous plants cultivated in temperate and subtropical regions. They are known for their bright flavor, juicy texture, and high levels of vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Berries are rich in anthocyanins, which give them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
There are over 2,000 edible berry species, including strawberry, raspberry, blueberry, currant, and cranberry.
Berries can grow wild or on cultivated farms where specific harvesting and processing methods are applied.
Berry seasons vary: some ripen early summer, others in the autumn.
Berries are widely used in jams, juices, desserts, and beverages.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low-calorie food
items.content: Berries provide nutrients without significantly increasing caloric intake.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular berry consumption is linked to improved lipid profiles and lower blood pressure.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergies to specific berry varieties.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improper handling can leave chemical residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet berries can raise blood glucose levels in people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Highly acidic berries may irritate the stomach lining when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Berries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, cereals, smoothies, baked goods, or used to make sauces and jams. Freezing preserves most of their nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store berries in the refrigerator in their original packaging or a ventilated container. For long‑term storage, freeze them. Remove any spoiled berries to prevent the rest from deteriorating.
